Appearance:
 Shri Rajmani Bansal - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Samar Ghuraiya - Public Prosecutor for the State.

Order 
Case diary is perused.

This is the second application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS/439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail relating to Crime No.278 of 2024 registered at Police Station - Purani Chawni , District - Gwalior (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 304-B, 498-A, 34 of IPC.

As per the case of prosecution, Gabbar Singh Kirar reported to SHO, Police Station Purani Chhawani, Gwalior that his daughter-in-law Rubi has hung herself in her room with the ceiling fan on 25.05.2024.
When police reached the residence of Gabbar Singh Kirar, Rubi was found hanging from ceiling fan.
Her dead body was forwarded for post mortem examination.
Medical Officer opined that Rubi has died due to asphyxia caused by hanging.

Statements of witnesses were recorded under Section 174 Cr.P.C. Urmila (mother), Suraj Singh Kirar (brother), Darshan Lal Kirar (father) who NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:17079 2 MCRC-22305-2025 stated that Rubi was married to Pradeep @ Dabbu Kirar S/o Gabbar Singh Kirar on 21.05.2023. Two- three months after her marriage, Dabbu @ Pradeep (husband of Rubi), Gabbar Singh (father-in-law),
Bharti (mother- inlaw) and child in conflict with law (sister-in-law)
started harassing her for demand of CRETA vehicle.
When Rubi came to her parental home, she informed her family members that her husband, father-in-law, mother-in-law and sister-in-law are harassing her.

sentences.text: On 25.05.2024, they called Gabbar Singh and Suraj Singh and asked them not to harass Rubi but Gabbar Singh said they would beat Rubi until their demand is fulfilled.
Soon thereafter, they received intimation that Rubi has committed suicide.
When they reached matrimonial home of Rubi, her husband and in-laws had escaped.
The rituals and final rites of Rubi were performed at her parental home.

On such allegations, Police Station Purani Chhawani, District Gwalior registered FIR at Crime No.278 of 2023 for commission of offence punishable under Section 304B, 498A, 34 of IPC against Pradeep @ Dabbu Kirar, Gabbar Singh Kirar, Bharti Devi (applicant) and child in conflict with law.
Statements of witnesses have been recorded.
Pradeep Kirar has been arrested on 12.07.2024.
Investigation is underway.
Applicant is apprehending arrest in the matter.

Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted before this Court that the present second bail application is being moved on the ground of changed circumstances, as subsequent to the rejection of the earlier bail application, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has been pleased to grant bail to father-in-law and mother-in-law of the deceased, who are co-accused in the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:17079 3 MCRC-22305-2025 same case and against whom similar allegations have been made.
It is further submitted that there is no material distinction in the role attributed to the applicant as compared to that of the co-accused who have already been granted bail.
The applicant is in custody since 12.07.2024.
Trial will take its own time.
The applicant undertakes to remain present before the trial Court on all dates and would not tamper with the evidence or influence any witnesses.
The applicant undertakes to cooperate in trial proceedings and abide by any condition imposed by the Court.
Hence, in light of the changed circumstances, the applicant prays to be enlarged on bail.

Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor for the State opposed the application and prayed for its rejection by contending that on the basis of the allegations and the material available on record, no case for grant of bail is made out.

Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record, it is evident that the present second bail application has been filed on the ground of changed circumstances.

It is specifically brought to the notice of this Court that, subsequent to the rejection of the applicant's earlier bail application, the Apex Court has granted bail to the applicant's father and mother, who are co-accused in the same case and against whom similar allegations have been levelled.
There appears to be no material distinction in the role attributed to the applicant and the said co-accused.
Further, there is no allegation of misuse of liberty by the co-accused who have already been released on bail.
The trial is likely to take considerable time.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:17079 4 MCRC-22305-2025

Considering the totality of facts and circumstances, the nature of allegations, the stage of trial, and the parity in role with the co-accused who have been granted bail, this Court is of the considered opinion that the applicant has made out a case for grant of bail.
Accordingly, the bail application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Pradeep Kirar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13288096/
2 Thousand only) with one solvent surety of like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, subject to the following conditions:
The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence or influence witnesses in any manner.
He shall appear before the trial Court on all dates fixed, without fail.
He shall not leave India without prior permission of the trial Court.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move for cancellation of bail.
Application stands disposed of.
CC as per Rules.
